definition: In artificial intelligence, the distributed multi-agent reasoning system (dMARS) was a platform for intelligent software agents developed at the AAII that makes uses of the belief–desire–intention software model (BDI).
details: The design for dMARS was an extension of the intelligent agent cognitive architecture developed at SRI International called procedural reasoning system (PRS). The most recent incarnation of this framework is the JACK Intelligent Agents platform.

explainer.lead: dMARS is a platform for building teams of intelligent software agents that reason through beliefs, desires, and intentions. It applies this goal-directed approach across multiple agents rather than treating the system as a single decision-maker.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a team of helpers where each one keeps track of what it knows, what jobs it wants to finish, and which job it has decided to do next. dMARS gives software helpers a way to work like that. Each helper can make its own plans while being part of a larger team.
tiers.practitioner: In this agent family, each agent’s reasoning is organized around beliefs, desires, and intentions, with dMARS providing the multi-agent platform. dMARS extends SRI International’s procedural reasoning system, while JACK Intelligent Agents is the framework’s most recent incarnation. A design pitfall is to adopt the BDI labels without clearly specifying what each agent believes, wants, and has committed to do.
tiers.paperLevel: dMARS is a distributed multi-agent platform based on the belief–desire–intention model: an agent’s reasoning is represented through beliefs, desires, and intentions, and multiple such agents form the system. It extends the procedural reasoning system (PRS) cognitive architecture developed at SRI International. Its lineage continues in JACK Intelligent Agents, the framework’s most recent incarnation.

explainer.example: Imagine three warehouse robots, each responsible for deliveries. One believes that its usual aisle is blocked, desires to deliver its assigned parcel, and forms the intention to take another route; the other robots reason separately about their own deliveries. Together they illustrate a distributed group of BDI agents rather than one agent making every decision.

usedIn.name: dMARS
usedIn.detail: An AAII platform for building intelligent software agents with the BDI model.

usedIn.name: JACK Intelligent Agents
usedIn.detail: The most recent incarnation of the agent framework that includes dMARS.

explainer.intuition: Give every software agent a practical model of decision-making: what it believes about its situation, what it wants to achieve, and what it intends to do. Distributing that model across agents lets a system contain many goal-directed decision-makers.
howItWorks: Represent an agent’s understanding of its situation as beliefs.
Represent the outcomes it may pursue as desires.
Use intentions to represent the courses of action it has chosen.
Apply this BDI reasoning across multiple agents in the distributed dMARS platform.
explainer.whyItMatters: dMARS connects a structured model of individual agent reasoning with systems containing many agents. It also forms an important link between the earlier PRS architecture and the later JACK Intelligent Agents platform.
misconceptions: dMARS is not PRS itself; its design extends the PRS cognitive architecture.
dMARS and JACK are not the same platform; JACK is the framework’s most recent incarnation.
BDI refers to beliefs, desires, and intentions, not merely to running software on several machines.
